## Findings

- **[P1] Edge fallback accepts malformed JSON Schemas.** [validation.ts:102](/Users/serro/orca/workspaces/superfunctions/mcp-4-make-mcpfn-cloudflare-worker-bundles-resil/mcpfn/core/src/validation.ts:102) assumes constructing `CfWorkerValidator` validates the schema itself, but that library does not perform meta-schema validation. With code generation disabled, schemas containing `minimum: "invalid"`, `required: "not-an-array"`, or an invalid regex were all accepted. Node/Ajv rejects them during registration. This lets invalid manifests and tool schemas reach production only on the advertised edge path.

- **[P1] The process-global Ajv instance makes independent registries interfere.** [validation.ts:40](/Users/serro/orca/workspaces/superfunctions/mcp-4-make-mcpfn-cloudflare-worker-bundles-resil/mcpfn/core/src/validation.ts:40) replaces each registry’s private Ajv instance with one shared instance. Registering two otherwise independent tools with the same legal `$id` succeeds for the first registry but makes the second throw `schema with key or id ... already exists`. Repeatedly validating separately parsed manifests has the same collision risk. Validator ownership needs to remain per registry/validation operation, or `$id` registrations must be isolated.

- **[P2] The new Worker gate does not exercise the fallback it claims to protect.** [test-mcpfn-cloudflare-worker.mjs:133](/Users/serro/orca/workspaces/superfunctions/mcp-4-make-mcpfn-cloudflare-worker-bundles-resil/scripts/test-mcpfn-cloudflare-worker.mjs:133) runs under the installed Miniflare/workerd configuration, where `new Function("return 42")()` succeeds. Consequently `codeGenerationAllowed` is true and the test continues using Ajv; it never executes the new `@cfworker/json-schema` branch. It also imports only `@mcpfn/core`, despite changing and advertising `@mcpfn/auth`. The gate therefore passes while the first finding remains undetected.

- **[P2] Advertised zero-configuration edge support silently requires `nodejs_compat`.** The gate explicitly enables it at [test-mcpfn-cloudflare-worker.mjs:136](/Users/serro/orca/workspaces/superfunctions/mcp-4-make-mcpfn-cloudflare-worker-bundles-resil/scripts/test-mcpfn-cloudflare-worker.mjs:136), while core statically imports Node crypto at [canonical.ts:1](/Users/serro/orca/workspaces/superfunctions/mcp-4-make-mcpfn-cloudflare-worker-bundles-resil/mcpfn/core/src/canonical.ts:1). Running the same bundle without that flag fails startup with `No such module "crypto"`, but the migration guide says “no configuration is required” at [MIGRATION.md:59](/Users/serro/orca/workspaces/superfunctions/mcp-4-make-mcpfn-cloudflare-worker-bundles-resil/mcpfn/MIGRATION.md:59). Either remove the Node-only import from the edge entry or document and enforce the compatibility flag.
